When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: CronCreate
tools.description:
Schedule a prompt to be enqueued at a future time. Use for both recurring schedules and one-shot reminders.

Uses standard 5-field cron in the user's local timezone: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. "0 9 * * *" means 9am local — no timezone conversion needed.

## One-shot tasks (recurring: false)

For "remind me at X" or "at <time>, do Y" requests — fire once then auto-delete.
Pin minute/hour/day-of-month/month to specific values:
  "remind me at 2:30pm today to check the deploy" → cron: "30 14 <today_dom> <today_month> *", recurring: false
  "tomorrow morning, run the smoke test" → cron: "57 8 <tomorrow_dom> <tomorrow_month> *", recurring: false

## Recurring jobs (recurring: true, the default)

For "every N minutes" / "every hour" / "weekdays at 9am" requests:
  "*/5 * * * *" (every 5 min), "0 * * * *" (hourly), "0 9 * * 1-5" (weekdays at 9am local)

## Avoid the :00 and :30 minute marks when the task allows it

Every user who asks for "9am" gets `0 9`, and every user who asks for "hourly" gets `0 *` — which means requests from across the planet land on the API at the same instant. When the user's request is approximate, pick a minute that is NOT 0 or 30:
  "every morning around 9" → "57 8 * * *" or "3 9 * * *" (not "0 9 * * *")
  "hourly" → "7 * * * *" (not "0 * * * *")
  "in an hour or so, remind me to..." → pick whatever minute you land on, don't round

Only use minute 0 or 30 when the user names that exact time and clearly means it ("at 9:00 sharp", "at half past", coordinating with a meeting). When in doubt, nudge a few minutes early or late — the user will not notice, and the fleet will.

## Durability

By default (durable: false) the job lives only in this Claude session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Claude exits. Pass durable: true to write to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json so the job survives restarts. Only use durable: true when the user explicitly asks for the task to persist ("keep doing this every day", "set this up permanently"). Most "remind me in 5 minutes" / "check back in an hour" requests should stay session-only.

## Runtime behavior

Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query). Durable jobs persist to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json and survive session restarts — on next launch they resume automatically. One-shot durable tasks that were missed while the REPL was closed are surfaced for catch-up. Session-only jobs die with the process. The scheduler adds a small deterministic jitter on top of whatever you pick: recurring tasks fire up to 10% of their period late (max 15 min); one-shot tasks landing on :00 or :30 fire up to 90 s early. Picking an off-minute is still the bigger lever.

Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

Returns a job ID you can pass to CronDelete.

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

tools.name: NotebookEdit
tools.description:
Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:
- You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing — this tool will fail otherwise.
- `notebook_path` must be an absolute path.
- `cell_id` is the `id` attribute shown in the Read tool's `<cell id="...">` output. It is required for `replace` and `delete`.
- `edit_mode` defaults to `replace`. Use `insert` to add a new cell after the cell with the given `cell_id` (or at the beginning of the notebook if `cell_id` is omitted) — `cell_type` is required when inserting. Use `delete` to remove the cell.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# AMR Dispatcher 容器入口脚本
#
# 职责
# ----
# 1. 源 ROS 2 Jazzy 环境与工作区 install/。
# 2. 按需 colcon 构建（接口包必须先构建，见下方说明）。
# 3. 无物理串口设备时，启动项目自带的 PTY 物理底盘模拟器，并把解析出的
#    /dev/pts/N 作为 serial_device 传给 launch。
# 4. 从工作区根目录启动 full_system.launch.py。
#
# 为什么必须 cd 到工作区根目录
# ---------------------------
# rest_gateway 与 dispatcher_visualizer_node 用相对路径加载静态资源：
#   rest_gateway.cpp:288            -> tools/operator_console.html
#   dispatcher_visualizer_node.cpp  -> config/stations.yaml
# 若工作目录不对，Web 控制台会 404，可视化节点会回退到 4 个硬编码默认站点。
#
# 用法
# ----
# 默认（自动构建 + 起模拟器 + 启动完整系统）:
#   docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.server.yml up -d
#
# 传参则直接执行该命令（跳过启动逻辑）:
#   docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD":/workspace amr-dispatcher:jazzy bash
#   docker run --rm    -v "$PWD":/workspace amr-dispatcher:jazzy bash -lc ./scripts/check_all.sh
#
# 环境变量
# --------
#   AMR_BUILD=1              强制重新构建
#   AMR_USE_MOCK_CHASSIS=1   无串口时启动 PTY 模拟器（默认 1）
#   AMR_SERIAL_DEVICE        指定串口设备（默认 /dev/ttyUSB0）
#   AMR_HEALTH_RATE_HZ       底盘健康/心跳发布频率（默认 5.0）
#   AMR_COLCON_WORKERS       colcon 并发数（默认 nproc；低内存机器建议设 1 或 2）

set -eo pipefail

ROS_DISTRO="${ROS_DISTRO:-jazzy}"
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "/opt/ros/${ROS_DISTRO}/setup.bash"

WORKSPACE="${AMR_WORKSPACE:-/workspace}"
cd "$WORKSPACE"

export ROS_DOMAIN_ID="${ROS_DOMAIN_ID:-42}"

log() { echo "[amr-entrypoint] $*"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 构建
need_build=0
if [ "${AMR_BUILD:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  need_build=1
elif [ ! -f install/setup.bash ]; then
  log "未发现 install/setup.bash，执行首次构建"
  need_build=1
fi

if [ "$need_build" = "1" ]; then
  workers="${AMR_COLCON_WORKERS:-$(nproc)}"
  log "开始 colcon 构建（并行度 $workers）"

  # --base-paths src 是必需的：仓库根目录有一个 CMakeLists.txt，若不加此参数
  # colcon 会把【整个仓库根】当成一个包（amr_dispatcher_workspace），转而忽略

        raw_serials = launch_config_value(context, 'serial_devices')

        nodes = []
        for idx, vid in enumerate(ids):

#### 1. `dispatcher_node` 是否已有封路服务
* **已存在完整服务**：

    * 请求：`string from_station`, `string to_station`, `string reason`

#### 2. REST Gateway 接入方案
在 `src/amr_dispatcher_tools/src/rest_gateway.cpp` 中新增端点：

     * 等待响应后返回 HTTP 200 或 409/500。

   * **方法**：`POST`
   * **现存实现参考**：`rest_gateway.cpp` 中已有上传地图并自动生成拓扑的实现（行 950~1098）：

#### 3. 如何保障在途任务（In-flight Missions）的安全？
当道路突然封锁或拓扑变更时，系统在核心库与 ROS 节点中已建立了一套严密的安全防护体系（主要位于 `in_flight_reroute_planning.hpp/.cpp` 及 `dispatcher_node.cpp`）：

1. **两阶段资源置换原则（Two-Phase Lock Exchange）**：
   * 在途任务由 `PlanInFlightReroute` 进行重规划，输出 `new_required_locks`（新路线所需锁）与 `obsolete_locks`（旧路线上未来未驶入的废弃锁）。
   * **铁律**：必须**先成功预约并锁住所有 `new_required_locks`**，之后**才允许释放 `obsolete_locks`**。严禁先放锁后申请，防止新路径锁申请失败导致车辆在原地悬空无路权。
2. **当前安全立足点保护（Current Anchor Protection）**：
   * 重规划的起点**必须是车辆当前已经安全停靠的节点或当前所占用的节点**（`current_safe_node`）。
   * 该节点及车辆当前物理占用的资源锁绝对不允许进入 `obsolete_locks`，确保即使重规划失败或在计算期间，车辆的物理安全立足点绝不会被释放或被抢占。
3. **不可伪造路径与降级停车（Fail-Safe Stopping）**：
   * 若封路后没有可行绕行路径（`Outcome::kNoAlternative`），系统绝不伪造跨越路径，而是触发安全降级：
     * 保持当前安全节点的占用；
     * 通过 `PublishStopPathForMission` 向底盘/导航栈下发空路径或紧急制动指令；
     * 保持报警状态（`kBlockedWaiting`），等待人工调度干预或路况解除。
4. **实时死锁与冲突再检测**：
   * 封路生效后，`deadlock_timer_` 定时调用 `DetectTrafficDeadlock`。如果绕行导致局部环路拥堵，死锁协调器（`TrafficRecoveryCoordinator`）会介入，挑选低优先级任务进行重规划或抢占取消，保证全局车流安全。</result>

#### 3. 如何保障在途任务（In-flight Missions）的安全？
当道路突然封锁或拓扑变更时，系统在核心库与 ROS 节点中已建立了一套严密的安全防护体系（主要位于 `in_flight_reroute_planning.hpp/.cpp` 及 `dispatcher_node.cpp`）：

1. **两阶段资源置换原则（Two-Phase Lock Exchange）**：
   * 在途任务由 `PlanInFlightReroute` 进行重规划，输出 `new_required_locks`（新路线所需锁）与 `obsolete_locks`（旧路线上未来未驶入的废弃锁）。
   * **铁律**：必须**先成功预约并锁住所有 `new_required_locks`**，之后**才允许释放 `obsolete_locks`**。严禁先放锁后申请，防止新路径锁申请失败导致车辆在原地悬空无路权。
2. **当前安全立足点保护（Current Anchor Protection）**：
   * 重规划的起点**必须是车辆当前已经安全停靠的节点或当前所占用的节点**（`current_safe_node`）。

3. **不可伪造路径与降级停车（Fail-Safe Stopping）**：

     * 保持报警状态（`kBlockedWaiting`），等待人工调度干预或路况解除。
4. **实时死锁与冲突再检测**：
   * 封路生效后，`deadlock_timer_` 定时调用 `DetectTrafficDeadlock`。如果绕行导致局部环路拥堵，死锁协调器（`TrafficRecoveryCoordinator`）会介入，挑选低优先级任务进行重规划或抢占取消，保证全局车流安全。</result>

colcon build \
    "${BASE_ARGS[@]}" \
    --packages-select amr_dispatcher_bt amr_dispatcher_ros amr_dispatcher_tools \
    --parallel-workers "$workers" \
    --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

  # 注意：此处不能用 `ros2 pkg list | grep -c`，因为 `source install/setup.bash`
  # 的输出会混入 grep，计数会偏低（实测 5 个包被数成 2 个）。
  # 直接看 install/ 目录更可靠。
  installed=$(find install -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'amr_dispatcher_*' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  log "构建完成，install/ 下已安装 $installed 个项目包"
fi

if [ -f install/setup.bash ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source install/setup.bash
fi

# ------------------------------------------------- 传入命令则直接执行
if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
  exec "$@"
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------- PTY 底盘模拟器
SERIAL_DEVICE="${AMR_SERIAL_DEVICE:-/dev/ttyUSB0}"
HEALTH_RATE_HZ="${AMR_HEALTH_RATE_HZ:-5.0}"
MOCK_PID=""

cleanup() {
  if [ -n "$MOCK_PID" ] && kill -0 "$MOCK_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    log "停止 PTY 底盘模拟器 (pid=$MOCK_PID)"
    kill "$MOCK_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$MOCK_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

if [ "${AMR_USE_MOCK_CHASSIS:-1}" = "1" ] && [ ! -e "$SERIAL_DEVICE" ]; then
  log "$SERIAL_DEVICE 不存在，启动 PTY 物理底盘模拟器"

  if [ ! -f scripts/mock_physical_chassis.py ]; then
    log "WARN 找不到 scripts/mock_physical_chassis.py，跳过模拟器"
  else
    MOCK_LOG="$(mktemp)"
    # -u 关闭 Python 输出缓冲。不加这个参数时，stdout 重定向到文件会变为块缓冲
    # （默认 8KB），而脚本启动日志只有几百字节，导致解析端在轮询窗口内读不到任何
    # 内容，误判为"未能解析 PTY"，底盘拿不到串口设备。
    python3 -u scripts/mock_physical_chassis.py >"$MOCK_LOG" 2>&1 &
    MOCK_PID=$!

    # 轮询模拟器输出，解析它创建的 PTY 从设备路径
    PTY=""
    for _ in $(seq 1 120); do
      PTY="$(grep -oE '/dev/pts/[0-9]+' "$MOCK_LOG" 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)"
      if [ -n "$PTY" ] && [ -e "$PTY" ]; then
        break
      fi
      PTY=""
      if ! kill -0 "$MOCK_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
        log "WARN 模拟器进程已退出，输出如下："
        cat "$MOCK_LOG" || true
        break
      fi
      sleep 0.25
    done

    if [ -n "$PTY" ]; then
      SERIAL_DEVICE="$PTY"
      log "模拟器就绪，serial_device=$SERIAL_DEVICE"
    else
      log "WARN 未能解析模拟器 PTY，沿用 $SERIAL_DEVICE（底盘将无数据，但心跳仍正常）"
    fi
  fi
else
  log "使用物理串口设备 $SERIAL_DEVICE"
fi

# -------------------------------------------------------------- 启动
log "启动完整系统（工作目录 $PWD，ROS_DOMAIN_ID=$ROS_DOMAIN_ID）"
ros2 launch launch/full_system.launch.py \
  serial_device:="$SERIAL_DEVICE" \
  health_rate_hz:="$HEALTH_RATE_HZ"

# 云服务器部署配置（AMR Dispatcher 完整系统）
#
# 这是本仓库唯一的 compose 配置。旧的 docker/docker-compose.yml 与
# docker/Dockerfile 已删除（它们依赖未随仓库分发的 robot-amr:latest 基础镜像）。
#
# 关键设计
# -------------------------------------------------
# 1. 用 bridge 网络 + "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"，替代 network_mode: host。
#    原因：rest_gateway.cpp:106 硬编码绑定 INADDR_ANY(0.0.0.0) 且没有 bind 地址
#    参数，且该应用无任何认证机制。host 网络下无法用 ports 限制绑定地址，端口会
#    直接暴露到公网；bridge + 回环绑定后，即使云安全组配错，8080 也只在服务器
#    本机可达，配合 SSH 隧道使用。
#    所有节点都跑在这一个容器内，DDS 通信不跨容器，bridge 网络完全够用。
#
# 2. 去掉 privileged: true 与 - /dev:/dev。容器内自带 PTY 模拟器提供底盘数据，
#    不需要访问宿主设备树，也不需要有特权。
#
# 3. working_dir 固定为 /workspace。rest_gateway 与 dispatcher_visualizer_node 用
#    相对路径加载 tools/operator_console.html 和 config/stations.yaml，工作目录
#    不对会导致 Web 控制台 404、可视化回退到硬编码站点。
#
# 4. 不含 build: 段。服务器可用内存仅 1.4GiB，在此编译 ROS 2 C++ 有 OOM 风险。
#    镜像应在开发机构建后传输加载（见 docs/DEPLOYMENT.md）。
#
# 用法（在 docker/ 目录下）：
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.server.yml up -d
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.server.yml logs -f
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.server.yml down

# 显式指定项目名，隔离本栈与同目录下的其他 compose 项目。
#
# compose 默认用目录名当项目名，本文件所在目录是 docker/，项目名因此为 "docker"。
# 若服务器上恰好也有其他 compose 栈使用同名项目（实测存在 tc_fcgi_app /
# tc_fcgi_nginx_fastdfs / tc_fcgi_mysql 三个容器同属 "docker" 项目），则
# `docker compose ... up -d --remove-orphans` 或 `down --remove-orphans`
# 会把这些无关容器一并删除。显式命名后本栈完全独立。
name: amr-dispatcher

services:
  amr_dispatcher:
    image: amr-dispatcher:jazzy
    container_name: amr_dispatcher
    restart: unless-stopped

    working_dir: /workspace
    volumes:
      # 仓库根目录（compose 文件的上一级）挂载为 /workspace。
      # 首次启动会在此生成 build/ install/ log/。
      - ../:/workspace

    ports:
      # 仅绑定回环。必须配合 SSH 隧道访问，公网不可达。
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"

    environment:
      - ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42
      # 无物理串口时自动启动 PTY 底盘模拟器（入口脚本负责解析 /dev/pts/N）
      - AMR_USE_MOCK_CHASSIS=1
      # 心跳周期 200ms，显著小于 safety_gate_node 的 heartbeat_timeout_ms=500ms，
      # 避免"心跳间隔 == 超时阈值"导致的看门狗误触发
      - AMR_HEALTH_RATE_HZ=5.0
      # 服务器 4 核，首次构建限 2 并发以控制内存峰值
      - AMR_COLCON_WORKERS=2

    # Fast DDS 走共享内存，默认 64MB 偏小
    shm_size: 512m

    # 限制容器日志增长，避免占满 17GB 可用磁盘
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "10m"
        max-file: "3"
docker-compose.server.yml
Dockerfile.jazzy
entrypoint.server.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
# check_metrics_e2e.sh - /metrics 端点验收（Prometheus 文本格式）
#
# 断言目标：抓取端拿到的是**合法** exposition，而不是一段看起来像指标的文本：
#   * Content-Type 是 text/plain; version=0.0.4
#   * 每个指标都有 # HELP / # TYPE，且 TYPE 只取 gauge / counter
#   * 每行样本都能被 `name{label="value"} number` 完整匹配（标签值已转义）
#   * 数值不是科学计数法、不是空、不是 NaN（本场景所有指标都是有限值）
#   * 无受管车时**不**产生空族（没有 amr_vehicle_online 的 HELP 行）
#   * 网关自身请求计数可自证：请求过 401 与 200 后，两个 code 都有样本
#   * metrics_token 独立生效：/metrics 用 metrics_token，业务端点仍用 auth_token
#
# 环境隔离：ROS_DOMAIN_ID=88 / REST 18099，不属于生产（42 / 8080），也不与
#           其它 e2e（77/78/80/82/84/86/87）重叠。只起 rest_gateway，
#           不依赖 dispatcher（无 DispatcherState 时指标应退化为 0 而不是崩溃）。
#
# 退出码：0 = 全部通过；非 0 = 断言失败（现场保留在容器 /tmp 便于排查）
# ==============================================================================
set -eo pipefail
set -E
trap 'echo "[METRICS-FATAL] line=${LINENO} status=$? cmd=${BASH_COMMAND}" >&2' ERR

CONTAINER="${AMR_METRICS_CONTAINER:-amr_dispatcher}"
METRICS_DOMAIN_ID="${AMR_METRICS_DOMAIN_ID:-88}"
METRICS_PORT="${AMR_METRICS_PORT:-18099}"
CONTAINER_WORKDIR="${AMR_METRICS_WORKDIR:-/workspace}"
AUTH_TOKEN="metrics-e2e-auth-token"
METRICS_TOKEN="metrics-e2e-scrape-token"
ASSERT_SCRIPT="$(mktemp -t amr_metrics_assert_XXXXXX.py)"

for tool in docker python3; do
    command -v "${tool}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
        echo "[METRICS-FAIL] 宿主机缺少必需工具: ${tool}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
done
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx "${CONTAINER}" || {
    echo "[METRICS-FAIL] 容器 ${CONTAINER} 未运行" >&2
    exit 2
}

# 生产红线：域 42 / 端口 8080 绝不触碰
if [ "${METRICS_DOMAIN_ID}" = "42" ] || [ "${METRICS_PORT}" = "8080" ]; then
    echo "[METRICS-FAIL] 拒绝使用生产域/端口 (42 / 8080)" >&2
    exit 2
fi

cleanup() {
    rm -f "${ASSERT_SCRIPT}"
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c \
        "pkill -f 'rest_gateway.*port:=${METRICS_PORT}' 2>/dev/null; true" || true
}
trap 'cleanup' EXIT

echo "[Metrics] 容器 ${CONTAINER} / 域 ${METRICS_DOMAIN_ID} / 端口 ${METRICS_PORT}"

# ---- 0. 清扫同域遗留 ----
docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "
    for envf in /proc/[0-9]*/environ; do
        pid=\${envf#/proc/}; pid=\${pid%/environ}
        [ -r \"\$envf\" ] || continue
        if tr '\\0' '\\n' 2>/dev/null < \"\$envf\" | grep -qx 'ROS_DOMAIN_ID=${METRICS_DOMAIN_ID}'; then
            kill -KILL \"\$pid\" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
    done
    true
"
echo "[Metrics] 已清扫域 ${METRICS_DOMAIN_ID} 的遗留进程"

# ---- 1. 起网关（metrics_token 与 auth_token 刻意不同）----
docker exec -d "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "
    export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=${METRICS_DOMAIN_ID}
    source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
    source ${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}/install/setup.bash
    exec ros2 run amr_dispatcher_tools rest_gateway --ros-args \
        -p port:=${METRICS_PORT} \
        -p auth_token:=${AUTH_TOKEN} \
        -p metrics_token:=${METRICS_TOKEN}
"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
# check_rest_gateway_hardening.sh - REST 网关健壮性与安全边界验收
#
# 目标：把"已复现的网关缺陷"变成可复现的回归断言。旧网关在这台机器上实测：
#   * 发一个 `Content-Length: abc` -> terminate called after throwing an
#     instance of 'std::invalid_argument' -> 整个网关进程 abort
#   * `prio=notanumber` -> 同上
#   * 建连后不发数据 -> 后续所有请求超时（单线程同步 accept 被卡死）
#
# 本脚本只依赖 python3（标准库 socket），不需要 netcat / curl 之外的额外工具；
# 全部请求走裸 socket，能构造 curl 不会发的畸形报文。
#
# 环境隔离：ROS_DOMAIN_ID=86 / REST 18096，与生产（域 42 / 8080）及其它 e2e
#           （77/78/80/82/84）完全隔离。不启动 dispatcher：本脚本验的是
#           **网关自身的边界**，后端服务缺失时应回 503 而不是崩溃。
#
# 退出码：0 = 全部断言通过；非 0 = 有断言失败（现场保留在 /tmp 便于排查）
# ==============================================================================
set -eo pipefail
set -E
trap 'echo "[HARD-FATAL] line=${LINENO} status=$? cmd=${BASH_COMMAND}" >&2' ERR

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

CONTAINER="${AMR_HARD_CONTAINER:-amr_dispatcher}"
HARD_DOMAIN_ID="${AMR_HARD_DOMAIN_ID:-86}"
HARD_PORT="${AMR_HARD_PORT:-18096}"
HARD_AUTH_PORT="${AMR_HARD_AUTH_PORT:-18097}"
CONTAINER_WORKDIR="${AMR_HARD_WORKDIR:-/workspace}"
STAMP_DIR="${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}/.hard_stamp"

HARD_FAILED=0

for tool in docker python3; do
    command -v "${tool}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
        echo "[HARD-FAIL] 宿主机缺少必需工具: ${tool}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
done
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx "${CONTAINER}" || {
    echo "[HARD-FAIL] 容器 ${CONTAINER} 未运行" >&2
    exit 2
}

fail() {
    echo ""
    echo "[HARD-FAIL] 验收失败: $1"
    echo "--- [LOG TAIL: gateway (no-auth)] ---"
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "tail -n 40 '${STAMP_DIR}/gateway.log' 2>/dev/null" || echo "(no log)"

    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "tail -n 20 '${STAMP_DIR}/gateway_auth.log' 2>/dev/null" || echo "(no log)"
    HARD_FAILED=1
    exit 1
}

cleanup() {
    local exit_code=$?
    echo ""

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
# check_state_persistence_e2e.sh - 调度状态持久化与审计落盘验收
#
# 断言（对应批次 2 的验收标准）：
#   1. 提交 3 单 -> 触发落盘 -> kill -9 调度器 -> 重启 -> 队列仍在
#   2. next_sequence 不回退（重启后新任务序号 > 已见最大序号）
#   3. 暂停订单的暂停标记跨重启保留（暂停单不出队、不丢单）
#   4. 隔离车辆跨重启保留（重启后仍是隔离态，不参与自动分配）
#   5. 审计文件包含强清记录（operator_id / reason / released_resources）
#   6. map_hash 不匹配时**拒绝恢复**（不允许拿旧拓扑的队列去派发）
#
# 环境隔离：ROS_DOMAIN_ID=87 / REST 18098 / MQTT 18891，与生产（域 42 / 8080）
#           及其它 e2e（77/78/80/82/86/88）完全隔离。
#
# 退出码：0 = 全部断言通过；非 0 = 有断言失败（现场保留在容器 /tmp 便于排查）
# ==============================================================================
set -eo pipefail
set -E
trap 'echo "[PERS-FATAL] line=${LINENO} status=$? cmd=${BASH_COMMAND}" >&2' ERR

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

CONTAINER="${AMR_PERS_CONTAINER:-amr_dispatcher}"
PERS_DOMAIN_ID="${AMR_PERS_DOMAIN_ID:-87}"
PERS_REST_PORT="${AMR_PERS_REST_PORT:-18098}"
PERS_MQTT_PORT="${AMR_PERS_MQTT_PORT:-18891}"
CONTAINER_WORKDIR="${AMR_PERS_WORKDIR:-/workspace}"
STAMP_DIR="${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}/.pers_stamp"

PERS_FAILED=0

for tool in docker python3; do
    command -v "${tool}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
        echo "[PERS-FAIL] 宿主机缺少必需工具: ${tool}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
done
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx "${CONTAINER}" || {
    echo "[PERS-FAIL] 容器 ${CONTAINER} 未运行" >&2
    exit 2
}

fail() {
    echo ""
    echo "[PERS-FAIL] 验收失败: $1"
    echo "--- [LOG TAIL: dispatcher] ---"
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "tail -n 60 '${STAMP_DIR}/dispatcher.log' 2>/dev/null" || echo "(no log)"
    echo "--- [SNAPSHOT] ---"
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "cat '${STAMP_DIR}/dispatch_state.yaml' 2>/dev/null" || echo "(no snapshot)"
    echo "--- [AUDIT] ---"
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "tail -n 20 '${STAMP_DIR}/audit.jsonl' 2>/dev/null" || echo "(no audit)"
    PERS_FAILED=1
    exit 1
}

cleanup() {
    local exit_code=$?
    echo ""
    echo "[PERS] 正在清理..."
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "
        for envf in /proc/[0-9]*/environ; do
            pid=\"\${envf#/proc/}\"; pid=\"\${pid%/environ}\"
            [ -r \"\${envf}\" ] || continue
            if tr '\\0' '\\n' 2>/dev/null < \"\${envf}\" | grep -qx 'ROS_DOMAIN_ID=${PERS_DOMAIN_ID}'; then
                kill -9 \"\${pid}\" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
        done
        pkill -9 -f '[r]est_gateway.*port:=${PERS_REST_PORT}' 2>/dev/null || true
        pkill -9 -f '[m]osquitto -c ${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}/.pers_stamp/mosquitto.conf' 2>/dev/null || true
        pkill -9 -f '[m]ock_vda5050_vehicle.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PERS_MQTT_PORT}' 2>/dev/null || true
        ROS_DOMAIN_ID=${PERS_DOMAIN_ID} bash -c 'source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash >/dev/null 2>&1; ros2 daemon stop >/dev/null 2>&1' || true
    " >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    if [ ${exit_code} -eq 0 ] && [ ${PERS_FAILED} -eq 0 ]; then
        docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "rm -rf '${STAMP_DIR}'" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        echo "[PERS] 全部通过，已清理临时现场"
    else
        echo "[PERS][WARN] 验收未全部成功，现场保留在容器内: ${STAMP_DIR}"
    fi
    exit ${exit_code}
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

STATIONS_YAML="${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}/config/generated/stations.yaml"
docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "test -f '${STATIONS_YAML}'" \
    || fail "容器内缺少 ${STATIONS_YAML}（先跑 check_map_ingest_e2e.sh 生成拓扑）"
MAP_HASH="$(docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "grep -oE 'fnv1a64_[0-9a-f]+' '${STATIONS_YAML}' | head -1" | tr -d '\r')"
[ -n "${MAP_HASH}" ] || fail "无法从 stations.yaml 提取 map_hash"

docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "rm -rf '${STAMP_DIR}' && mkdir -p '${STAMP_DIR}'"

echo "======================================================================"
echo " Dispatch State Persistence End-to-End Acceptance"
echo " ROS_DOMAIN_ID: ${PERS_DOMAIN_ID}  REST: ${PERS_REST_PORT}  MQTT: ${PERS_MQTT_PORT}"
echo " map_hash: ${MAP_HASH}"
echo "======================================================================"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 容器内栈脚本：mosquitto + dispatcher(开启持久化) + gateway + rest + mock 车
# 参数 $1 = 快照/审计路径前缀（不同轮次用不同文件）
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
write_stack_script() {
    local snapshot_extra="$1"   # 追加的 -p 参数（如 expected_map_hash 覆盖）
    cat > /tmp/pers_stack.sh <<INNER
set -eo pipefail
cd "${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}"
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}/install/setup.bash"
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=${PERS_DOMAIN_ID}
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
STAMP="${STAMP_DIR}"

cat > "\${STAMP}/mosquitto.conf" <<EOF
listener ${PERS_MQTT_PORT} 127.0.0.1
allow_anonymous true
EOF
mosquitto -c "\${STAMP}/mosquitto.conf" -v > "\${STAMP}/mosq.log" 2>&1 &
sleep 1

    echo "--- [LOG TAIL: dispatcher] ---"
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "tail -n 60 '${STAMP_DIR}/dispatcher.log' 2>/dev/null" || echo "(no log)"
    echo "--- [SNAPSHOT] ---"
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "cat '${STAMP_DIR}/dispatch_state.yaml' 2>/dev/null" || echo "(no snapshot)"
    echo "--- [AUDIT] ---"
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "tail -n 20 '${STAMP_DIR}/audit.jsonl' 2>/dev/null" || echo "(no audit)"
    PERS_FAILED=1
    exit 1
}

cleanup() {
    local exit_code=$?
    echo ""
    echo "[PERS] 正在清理..."
    docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "
        for envf in /proc/[0-9]*/environ; do
            pid=\"\${envf#/proc/}\"; pid=\"\${pid%/environ}\"
            [ -r \"\${envf}\" ] || continue
            if tr '\\0' '\\n' 2>/dev/null < \"\${envf}\" | grep -qx 'ROS_DOMAIN_ID=${PERS_DOMAIN_ID}'; then
                kill -9 \"\${pid}\" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
        done

        pkill -9 -f '[m]osquitto -c ${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}/.pers_stamp/mosquitto.conf' 2>/dev/null || true
        pkill -9 -f '[m]ock_vda5050_vehicle.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PERS_MQTT_PORT}' 2>/dev/null || true
        ROS_DOMAIN_ID=${PERS_DOMAIN_ID} bash -c 'source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash >/dev/null 2>&1; ros2 daemon stop >/dev/null 2>&1' || true

    if [ ${exit_code} -eq 0 ] && [ ${PERS_FAILED} -eq 0 ]; then
        docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "rm -rf '${STAMP_DIR}'" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        echo "[PERS] 全部通过，已清理临时现场"
    else
        echo "[PERS][WARN] 验收未全部成功，现场保留在容器内: ${STAMP_DIR}"
    fi
    exit ${exit_code}
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

STATIONS_YAML="${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}/config/generated/stations.yaml"
docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "test -f '${STATIONS_YAML}'" \
    || fail "容器内缺少 ${STATIONS_YAML}（先跑 check_map_ingest_e2e.sh 生成拓扑）"

[ -n "${MAP_HASH}" ] || fail "无法从 stations.yaml 提取 map_hash"

docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "rm -rf '${STAMP_DIR}' && mkdir -p '${STAMP_DIR}'"

echo "======================================================================"
echo " Dispatch State Persistence End-to-End Acceptance"
echo " ROS_DOMAIN_ID: ${PERS_DOMAIN_ID}  REST: ${PERS_REST_PORT}  MQTT: ${PERS_MQTT_PORT}"
echo " map_hash: ${MAP_HASH}"
echo "======================================================================"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 容器内栈脚本：mosquitto + dispatcher(开启持久化) + gateway + rest + mock 车
# 参数 $1 = 快照/审计路径前缀（不同轮次用不同文件）

cd "${CONTAINER_WORKDIR}"
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash

cat > "\${STAMP}/mosquitto.conf" <<EOF
listener ${PERS_MQTT_PORT} 127.0.0.1
allow_anonymous true
EOF

sleep 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
WORKSPACE_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
REPORT_FILE="${WORKSPACE_DIR}/test_report_matrix.json"

START_TIME=$(date +%s)

echo "================================================================="
echo "       AMR Dispatcher 工业级系统基础设施与混沌演练流水线         "
echo "================================================================="

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 阶段状态一律由实际执行结果生成：PASSED / FAILED / SKIPPED。
#   PASSED  = 阶段执行成功
#   FAILED  = 阶段执行失败（计入失败数，脚本最终以非零退出）
#   SKIPPED = 本机不具备执行条件（不计入失败，但如实写入报告与 verdict）
# 矩阵中不再写入任何硬编码的通过结论；verdict 只基于实际执行的阶段。
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CORE_STATUS="SKIPPED"
BENCH_STATUS="SKIPPED"
BT_STATUS="SKIPPED"
CHAOS_DEADLOCK_STATUS="SKIPPED"
CHAOS_WATCHDOG_STATUS="SKIPPED"
CHAOS_FAILOVER_STATUS="SKIPPED"
FAILED_STAGES=0

# record_status <目标变量名> <PASSED|FAILED>
record_status() {
  local -n _status_ref="$1"
  _status_ref="$2"
  if [ "$2" = "FAILED" ]; then
    FAILED_STAGES=$((FAILED_STAGES + 1))
  fi
}

# count_suites <目录...>：统计测试源码中唯一 TEST/TEST_F 套件名数量（无匹配时输出 0）
count_suites() {
  {
    grep -rhoE 'TEST(_F)?[[:space:]]*\([[:space:]]*[A-Za-z0-9_]+' "$@" 2>/dev/null \
      | sed -E 's/.*\([[:space:]]*//' \
      | sort -u \
      | wc -l \
      | tr -d '[:space:]'
  } || true
}

# count_ctest_cases <构建目录>：读取 ctest 注册的用例总数（仅列举不执行）
count_ctest_cases() {
  {
    ctest --test-dir "$1" -N 2>/dev/null \
      | sed -n 's/.*Total Tests: \([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' \
      | tail -1
  } || true
}

# json_number <值>：空值降级为 JSON null
json_number() {
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then printf '%s' "$1"; else printf 'null'; fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# L1 核心层：纯 C++ 编译 + GoogleTest
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "[L1 核心层] 编译纯 C++ 核心库并执行 GoogleTest 单元测试 (零 ROS 依赖)..."
if "${WORKSPACE_DIR}/scripts/build.sh"; then
  record_status CORE_STATUS PASSED
else
  echo "[L1 核心层] FAILED：构建或单测未通过" >&2
  record_status CORE_STATUS FAILED
fi

CORE_TEST_CASES=""
CORE_TEST_SUITES=""
if [ "$CORE_STATUS" = "PASSED" ]; then
  CORE_TEST_CASES="$(count_ctest_cases "${WORKSPACE_DIR}/build/core")"
  CORE_TEST_SUITES="$(count_suites "${WORKSPACE_DIR}/test/unit" "${WORKSPACE_DIR}/test/integration")"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# L1 压测层：基准压测（依赖 L1 构建产物）
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
BENCH_LOG="$(mktemp)"
# M6：脚本早退路径也要清理 benchmark 临时文件
trap 'rm -f "${BENCH_LOG}"' EXIT
BENCH_QUEUE_NOTE="not measured (benchmark stage not executed)"
BENCH_LOGGER_NOTE="not measured (benchmark stage not executed)"
if [ "$CORE_STATUS" = "PASSED" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "[L1 压测层] 执行核心库极限基准压测 (任务队列并发 & 异步低阻塞日志)..."
  if "${WORKSPACE_DIR}/scripts/benchmark.sh" 2>&1 | tee "${BENCH_LOG}"; then
    record_status BENCH_STATUS PASSED
  else
    echo "[L1 压测层] FAILED：基准压测未通过" >&2
    record_status BENCH_STATUS FAILED
  fi
  bench_queue_push="$(sed -n 's/.*Push throughput: \([0-9.]*\) ops\/sec.*/\1/p' "${BENCH_LOG}" | head -1)"
  bench_queue_pop="$(sed -n 's/.*Pop throughput:[[:space:]]*\([0-9.]*\) ops\/sec.*/\1/p' "${BENCH_LOG}" | head -1)"
  bench_logger="$(sed -n 's/.*Enqueue throughput: \([0-9.]*\) ops\/sec.*/\1/p' "${BENCH_LOG}" | head -1)"
  if [ "$BENCH_STATUS" = "PASSED" ]; then
    if [ -n "$bench_queue_push" ] && [ -n "$bench_queue_pop" ]; then
      BENCH_QUEUE_NOTE="push ${bench_queue_push} ops/sec, pop ${bench_queue_pop} ops/sec (measured this run)"
    fi
    if [ -n "$bench_logger" ]; then
      BENCH_LOGGER_NOTE="enqueue ${bench_logger} ops/sec (measured this run)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo ""
  echo "[L1 压测层] SKIPPED：依赖 L1 核心库构建产物"
fi
rm -f "${BENCH_LOG}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# L1 行为树层：amr_dispatcher_bt（ament/colcon 产物；纯宿主机无此产物则 SKIPPED）
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
BT_BUILD_DIR="${WORKSPACE_DIR}/build/amr_dispatcher_bt"
BT_TEST_CASES=""
BT_TEST_SUITES=""
if [ -d "${BT_BUILD_DIR}" ]; then
  # 构建产物可能来自 Docker 容器（CTestTestfile 内记录 /workspace 绝对路径），
  # 宿主机上这些路径不存在，ctest 必然报错——此时应判 SKIPPED 而非 FAILED。
  BT_FOREIGN_BUILD_DIR="$(sed -n 's/^# Build directory: //p' "${BT_BUILD_DIR}/CTestTestfile.cmake" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
  if [ -n "${BT_FOREIGN_BUILD_DIR}" ] && [ ! -d "${BT_FOREIGN_BUILD_DIR}" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "[L1 行为树层] SKIPPED：BT 构建产物来自容器（${BT_FOREIGN_BUILD_DIR} 在宿主机不存在），宿主机无法执行；请在容器/CI 内运行"
  else
    echo ""
    echo "[L1 行为树层] 执行 amr_dispatcher_bt 行为树单元测试 (BehaviorTree.CPP v4 + GTest)..."
    if ctest --test-dir "${BT_BUILD_DIR}" --output-on-failure; then
      record_status BT_STATUS PASSED
      BT_TEST_CASES="$(count_ctest_cases "${BT_BUILD_DIR}")"
      BT_TEST_SUITES="$(count_suites "${WORKSPACE_DIR}/src/amr_dispatcher_bt/test")"
    else
      echo "[L1 行为树层] FAILED：BT ctest 未通过" >&2
      record_status BT_STATUS FAILED
    fi
  fi
else
  echo ""
  echo "[L1 行为树层] SKIPPED：build/amr_dispatcher_bt 不存在（BT 包需 colcon/ament 构建，本环境未构建）"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# L3 场景层：混沌演练（依赖 L1 构建产物）
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$CORE_STATUS" = "PASSED" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "[L3 场景层: 混沌演练 1] 执行拓扑路网死锁检测与恢复演练..."
  if "${WORKSPACE_DIR}/scripts/check_deadlock_resolution.sh"; then
    record_status CHAOS_DEADLOCK_STATUS PASSED
  else
    echo "[L3 混沌演练 1] FAILED：死锁检测与恢复演练未通过" >&2
    record_status CHAOS_DEADLOCK_STATUS FAILED
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "[L3 场景层: 混沌演练 2] 执行软看门狗心跳丢失与安全门熔断制动演练..."
  if "${WORKSPACE_DIR}/scripts/check_watchdog_estop.sh"; then
    record_status CHAOS_WATCHDOG_STATUS PASSED
  else
    echo "[L3 混沌演练 2] FAILED：看门狗/急停演练未通过" >&2
    record_status CHAOS_WATCHDOG_STATUS FAILED
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "[L3 场景层: 混沌演练 3] 执行底层通信丢包监控与三级容灾降级演练..."
  if "${WORKSPACE_DIR}/scripts/check_hardware_failover.sh"; then
    record_status CHAOS_FAILOVER_STATUS PASSED
  else
    echo "[L3 混沌演练 3] FAILED：硬件降级演练未通过" >&2
    record_status CHAOS_FAILOVER_STATUS FAILED
  fi
else
  echo ""
  echo "[L3 场景层] SKIPPED：依赖 L1 核心库构建产物"
  CHAOS_DEADLOCK_STATUS="SKIPPED (依赖 L1)"
  CHAOS_WATCHDOG_STATUS="SKIPPED (依赖 L1)"
  CHAOS_FAILOVER_STATUS="SKIPPED (依赖 L1)"
fi

END_TIME=$(date +%s)
DURATION=$((END_TIME - START_TIME))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# verdict：只基于实际执行的阶段
#   FAILED                        —— 任一执行阶段失败
#   PASSED_WITH_SKIPPED_STAGES    —— 已执行阶段全过，但存在 SKIPPED 阶段
#   ALL_PASSED                    —— 全部阶段执行且全部通过
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ANY_SKIPPED=0
for _s in "$CORE_STATUS" "$BENCH_STATUS" "$BT_STATUS" \
          "$CHAOS_DEADLOCK_STATUS" "$CHAOS_WATCHDOG_STATUS" "$CHAOS_FAILOVER_STATUS"; do
  case "$_s" in
    SKIPPED*) ANY_SKIPPED=1 ;;
  esac
done

if [ "${FAILED_STAGES}" -gt 0 ]; then
  VERDICT="FAILED"
elif [ "${ANY_SKIPPED}" -eq 1 ]; then
  VERDICT="PASSED_WITH_SKIPPED_STAGES"
else
  VERDICT="ALL_PASSED"
fi

# 生成格式化测试矩阵交付报告（全部字段来自本次实际执行结果）
cat <<EOF > "${REPORT_FILE}"
{
  "project": "amr_dispatcher",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "timestamp": "$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")",
  "duration_seconds": ${DURATION},
  "testing_matrix": {
    "L1_core_unit_tests": {
      "status": "${CORE_STATUS}",
      "test_suites": $(json_number "${CORE_TEST_SUITES}"),
      "test_cases": $(json_number "${CORE_TEST_CASES}"),
      "dependencies": "Zero-ROS (Pure C++17/20 STL, GTest)",
      "note": "suites 源码实测统计, cases 取 ctest 实测注册数; 数字随测试增补而变化"
    },
    "L1_behavior_tree_tests": {
      "status": "${BT_STATUS}",
      "test_suites": $(json_number "${BT_TEST_SUITES}"),
      "test_cases": $(json_number "${BT_TEST_CASES}"),
      "framework": "BehaviorTree.CPP v4 + GTest",
      "note": "仅在 build/amr_dispatcher_bt 存在(colcon 构建过)时执行, 否则 SKIPPED"
    },
    "L1_performance_benchmark": {
      "status": "${BENCH_STATUS}",
      "mission_queue_throughput": "${BENCH_QUEUE_NOTE}",
      "async_logger_throughput": "${BENCH_LOGGER_NOTE}"
    },
    "L2_node_contracts": {
      "status": "SKIPPED",
      "reason": "无自动化执行框架: test/l2_launch_contracts 仅为脚本样例, 未接入 ctest/launch_testing",
      "framework": "ROS 2 launch_testing & Lifecycle Coordinator Probes (规划中)",
      "contracts": [
        "/system/ready",
        "/system/healthy",
        "ExecuteMission.action",
        "12 Core Dispatcher Services (/v2/*)"
      ]
    },
    "L3_chaos_scenarios": {
      "deadlock_wfg_cycle_resolution": "${CHAOS_DEADLOCK_STATUS}",
      "watchdog_200ms_timeout_cutoff": "${CHAOS_WATCHDOG_STATUS}",
      "hardware_failover_3tier_degradation": "${CHAOS_FAILOVER_STATUS}"
    }
  },
  "verdict": "${VERDICT}"
}
EOF

echo ""
echo "================================================================="
if [ "${FAILED_STAGES}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "  [FAILED] ${FAILED_STAGES} 个阶段失败，verdict=${VERDICT}，详见上方日志。"
  echo "  📄 测试报告（含失败状态）已写入: ${REPORT_FILE}"
  echo "================================================================="
  exit 1
fi
echo "  [ALL EXECUTED STAGES PASSED] verdict=${VERDICT}（SKIPPED 阶段以报告为准）"
echo "  📄 测试报告已固化至: ${REPORT_FILE}"
echo "================================================================="

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
L2 契约测试：生命周期协调与就绪探针（launch_testing 真断言）。

此前本文件只有 `assertTrue(True)`——它永远通过，因此"契约"实际上没有任何
约束力。这里改成对**真实进程**做可证伪的断言：

  1. 协调器启动后 `/system/ready`、`/system/healthy` 两个服务可调用
  2. auto_bringup=false 时 dispatcher 不被提拉 -> `/system/ready` 报
     ready=false 且 state=INITIALIZING（门禁语义：未就绪不放行）
  3. `/system/ready_flag`（transient_local）发布布尔量，且当前值为 false
  4. 关停时所有进程以 0 退出

用**三个节点**（coordinator + dispatcher + safety_gate）而不是只有两个：
就绪判定是 `dispatcher active AND 安全门健康`，缺了 safety_gate 时协调器会
永久停在 `DEGRADED`（安全门从未上报），那既不是"未就绪门禁"也不是我们要
锁定的语义。三个节点一起起，未就绪状态就退化成确定性的 `INITIALIZING`。

本测试在**独立的 ROS_DOMAIN_ID（默认 91）**下运行：默认域 0 上可能残留
上一次运行的同名节点（`ros2 node list` 会看到旧的 dispatcher），lifecycle
调用被路由到旧节点会让结论不可信。

运行时依赖：launch_ros / launch_testing / rclpy（CI 的 ros:jazzy-ros-base 镜像
已包含）。不依赖 map_server、MQTT 或任何文件系统状态。
"""

import os
import time
import unittest

import launch
import launch_ros.actions
import launch_testing.actions
import launch_testing.asserts
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from rclpy.qos import DurabilityPolicy, QoSProfile, ReliabilityPolicy

from amr_dispatcher_interfaces.srv import GetSystemReadiness
from std_msgs.msg import Bool


TEST_DOMAIN_ID = os.environ.get("AMR_L2_DOMAIN_ID", "91")


def _node(package, executable, name, parameters=None):
    return launch_ros.actions.Node(
        package=package,
        executable=executable,
        name=name,
        parameters=parameters or [],
        output="screen",
        # 每个节点显式带域 ID：launch_testing 的子进程不继承我们的环境改写，
        # 显式传参才能保证三个节点与探针在同一张图上。
        additional_env={"ROS_DOMAIN_ID": TEST_DOMAIN_ID},
    )


def generate_test_description():
    # auto_bringup=false：协调器只看不拉，dispatcher 停在 unconfigured，
    # 于是"未就绪"是确定性的（不依赖时序竞态）。
    coordinator_node = launch_ros.actions.Node(
        package="amr_dispatcher_ros",
        executable="lifecycle_coordinator_node",
        name="lifecycle_coordinator_node",
        parameters=[{"auto_bringup": False, "check_period_ms": 100}],
        output="screen",
        additional_env={"ROS_DOMAIN_ID": TEST_DOMAIN_ID},
    )
    dispatcher_node = _node(
        "amr_dispatcher_ros", "dispatcher_node", "dispatcher_node",
        [{"max_active_missions": 1}])
    # 安全门必须在场：缺了它协调器永远停在 DEGRADED（从未收到安全状态）
    safety_gate_node = _node(
        "amr_dispatcher_ros", "safety_gate_node", "safety_gate_node")

    return (
        launch.LaunchDescription(
            [coordinator_node, safety_gate_node, dispatcher_node,
             launch_testing.actions.ReadyToTest()]
        ),
        {"coordinator": coordinator_node, "dispatcher": dispatcher_node,
         "safety_gate": safety_gate_node},
    )


class TestLifecycleCoordinationContract(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        os.environ["ROS_DOMAIN_ID"] = TEST_DOMAIN_ID
        rclpy.init()
        cls.node = Node("l2_lifecycle_contract_probe")
        cls.ready_cli = cls.node.create_client(GetSystemReadiness, "/system/ready")
        cls.healthy_cli = cls.node.create_client(GetSystemReadiness, "/system/healthy")
        cls.ready_flags = []
        cls.node.create_subscription(
            Bool,
            "/system/ready_flag",
            lambda msg: cls.ready_flags.append(msg.data),
            QoSProfile(
                depth=1,
                reliability=ReliabilityPolicy.RELIABLE,
                durability=DurabilityPolicy.TRANSIENT_LOCAL,
            ),
        )

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()

    def _call(self, client, timeout_sec=10.0):
        self.assertTrue(
            client.wait_for_service(timeout_sec=timeout_sec),
            f"{client.srv_name} 服务未在 {timeout_sec}s 内出现",
        )
        future = client.call_async(GetSystemReadiness.Request())
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_sec
        while not future.done() and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            rclpy.spin_once(self.node, timeout_sec=0.1)

Good: `LifecycleNode` accepts **kwargs → Node → ExecuteProcess, so `respawn=True`, `respawn_delay`, `respawn_max_retries` work.

Now let me check how lifecycle node respawn behaves: when a LifecycleNode crashes and is respawned, it starts in unconfigured. The launch file's `configure_event` EmitEvent fires once at launch. The `activate_event` is a RegisterEventHandler on state transition events — will it fire again for the respawned process? OnStateTransition handler registered in launch listens for lifecycle events emitted by the launch system itself (the EmitEvent ChangeState). When change_state is emitted, launch_ros's lifecycle node action tracks the transition and emits an OnStateTransition event. So the activate_event handler will fire again whenever we re-emit CONFIGURE and it succeeds. But the initial configure_event fires only at launch start.

So for respawn, I need a periodic watchdog that re-issues configure/activate — which the lifecycle_coordinator_node already does (`auto_bringup_` promotes unconfigured→configure→inactive→activate every 500ms). Great: the coordinator already covers lifecycle bringup after respawn. That's the key insight: respawn + existing coordinator auto_bringup = recovery. But the coordinator only handles dispatcher_node. Good enough for the crash case reported.

However: will respawn of a lifecycle node reset the coordinator? Coordinator polls `/dispatcher_node/get_state` service; after respawn it will see unconfigured and promote. Good.

Also important: the coordinator currently returns early if the get_state service is not ready — fine.

Now the readiness probe: `/readyz` needs to actually check dispatcher_node state, safety severity, chassis link. The gateway already subscribes to /safety/state, /chassis/link_health, /dispatcher/state and has a readiness client to /system/ready. Two design options:
1. Gateway calls `/system/ready` srv and adds its own local staleness checks (message timestamps), returning 503 with component detail.
2. Add a new richer srv.

Gateway-local approach reuses existing subscriptions — clean and cheap. But "dispatcher_node missing" detection: /dispatcher/state staleness (500ms publish) is a direct liveness signal. Currently coordinator does NOT verify dispatcher liveness beyond service availability — actually if dispatcher node died, get_state service disappears, `service_is_ready()` returns false, so `current_dispatcher_state_` keeps the old value "active" — a stale latch! That's exactly the 8-day blind spot: coordinator would keep publishing ready_flag=true if safety is healthy. Actually in the incident, safety was CRITICAL so ready would be false; but the ready_flag publishes only `dispatcher_state == active`, which would remain stale "active" forever. So coordinator itself has a staleness bug: it never resets `current_dispatcher_state_` when the service disappears.

Fix: in CoordinatorTick, if get_state client not ready for > N ticks, set current_dispatcher_state_ = "unreachable"/"unknown" and publish ready=false. That's a core fix.

Also readiness must include: safety severity stuck CRITICAL (with "since" duration) and chassis link tier. Coordinator subscribes to /safety/state only (motion_allowed). Need link health subscription in coordinator too? Or do it in gateway. Given the user's ask is on the gateway `/healthz` (liveness) and `/readyz` (readiness) — the plan summary says implement in rest_gateway. I'll do both:
- Gateway `/healthz`: process-local — always 200 OK if the HTTP worker can serve (liveness of gateway process itself). Must be exempt from auth (k8s/docker probes don't send tokens).
- Gateway `/readyz`: aggregate: (a) dispatcher state message freshness, (b) safety severity + age, (c) chassis link health, (d) coordinator readiness srv (optional, with timeout). Return 503 + JSON component detail.

Now what about alerting? Webhook on persistent CRITICAL or node crash. Where? Gateway can own an alert dispatcher loop (worker thread with timer?) The gateway node is spun by rclcpp::spin in main; we can use a wall timer inside the node to check conditions and fire webhooks via a background thread, to avoid blocking the executor. Simpler: implement a small `AlertDispatcher` in tools with its own thread: checks readiness snapshot every N seconds, posts to webhook URL with JSON body, dedupe by alert fingerprint + repeat interval. Pure-function core part: alert state machine (decide whether to fire based on severity/duration/last-fired) in `amr_dispatcher_tools/include/amr_dispatcher_tools/alert_policy.hpp` — unit testable, HTTP POST via a small socket client.

But be careful about scope explosion. Let me consider what the user actually asked:
1. Process supervision + health probes + active alerts (production blind spot).
2. Online topology hot-update REST API with atomic connectivity validation & in-flight vehicle safety.

Both are big. I should design a coherent plan with clear phases and honest, verifiable E2E.

Let me now check what dependencies exist for writing stations.yaml back (atomic write with backup/rollback). And how to apply an in-memory topology override without overwriting generated file? The important design decision: hot_update should modify the *active* topology. Since the source of truth is stations.yaml (possibly generated by map_ingest, which would overwrite on next run), applying runtime edge state (blocked/one-way/enabled) is better as an *overlay* persisted in a separate operator overlay file, e.g. `config/generated/topology_overlay.yaml`, and merged at load. Hmm. But requirement says "原子校验连通性与在途车安全" and "上传新 markers.yaml / 新增临时施工禁行区 / 临时把某条边标为单向".

I think the cleanest design respecting the existing architecture:

**Topology overlay** (pure core): `catalog::TopologyOverlay` — a small struct with edge state changes (`block_edge`, `unblock_edge`, `set_oneway`, `restore_bidirectional`), plus temporary station additions (new markers) maybe. Applying overlay to a base catalog yields an effective catalog. Overlay persisted atomically to `config/generated/topology_overlay.yaml` with backup; loaded at startup (so restarts preserve construction zones). This avoids mutating the generated file (which map_ingest regenerates) and avoids touching geometry.

But "新增 markers.yaml / 新地图灰度" — full catalog replacement is the other half. Two operations:
- `POST /api/v1/topology/hot_update` body: full stations catalog (YAML or JSON) → validate → atomic write → swap. This covers "upload new markers.yaml / new map version".
- `POST /api/v1/topology/block_edge` / `unblock_edge` / `set_direction`: overlay operations.

Both need: (1) atomic validation (parse + ValidateStationCatalog + connectivity of all stations + edge endpoints exist), (2) in-flight safety arbitration.

For in-flight safety arbitration: for each active mission, compute route from its current safe node to dropoff under the *new* topology (FindRoutePathAvoiding with newly blocked edges or FindRoutePath over new catalog). If no path → reject the update with 409 listing affected vehicles and their current anchors, unless `force_after_reroute` or the operator chooses `mode=wait`? Better two-phase: 
- Phase A (dry-run/validate): returns `safe: false` with affected missions + proposed reroutes. 
- Phase B (commit): if all affected missions have alternative routes, perform two-phase lock exchange per mission (reserve new locks, then release obsolete), update mission_route_paths_, republish plan; only then commit the topology swap.

That's the "原子校验连通性与在途车安全" done properly, reusing `PlanInFlightReroute` + existing two-phase logic from DeadlockTick.

Where does this live? The topology swap must be atomic w.r.t. the dispatcher's single-threaded executor. Gateway writing the file + dispatcher reloading at 1 Hz is NOT atomic-with-arbitration: dispatcher could reject the file after gateway already committed, or worse, accept it while a mission is stranded. So we need `FindRoutePath` to support directional blocking: an `EdgeTraversalPolicy` — e.g. overlay `disabled_directions: set<pair<from,to>>` where a directed pair is closed. Dijkstra then skips an edge in that direction only.

struct TopologyOverlay {

## Feature A: Health probes + supervision + alerting

Current state:
- `/api/system/ready` in gateway → forwards to `/system/ready` service (coordinator). Returns 503 if not ready.
- Coordinator `EvaluateReadiness`: `is_ready = (current_dispatcher_state_ == "active") && safety_seen_ && safety_healthy_`. `healthy = safety_healthy_`.
  - Note: `current_dispatcher_state_` starts as "unknown" and only updates if the get_state service responds. If dispatcher_node dies, `service_is_ready()` false → `current_dispatcher_state_` **stays "active" forever** — this is the exact bug: stale state. So `/system/ready` would report ready=true forever after dispatcher dies. That's the blind spot.
- Gateway `HandleReadiness` only queries `/system/ready`. It doesn't check safety severity CRITICAL specifically, nor link health, nor staleness.

Design:
1. **Core pure functions** in `amr_dispatcher_core/health/` (or `workflow/`):
   - `HealthReport` / `EvaluateHealth(const HealthInput&)` — pure function taking: gateway uptime, dispatcher lifecycle state string + age of last successful get_state poll, safety severity string + age, safety motion_allowed, chassis link tier/health + age, coordinator present. Returns overall status (OK/DEGRADED/FAULT), per-component list with `{name, ok, detail}`.
   - `ComputeLiveness(now, last_loop_tick)` — trivial.
   - `AlertDecision`/`PlanAlert`: hysteresis + dedup for webhook alerting — pure function: given a series of health evaluations and a "cooldown" and "must persist for N consecutive ticks", emit at most one alert per incident, and a recovery notice. Testable 100% on host.

2. **Coordinator fix** (`lifecycle_coordinator_node.cpp`): track the age of the last successful `GetState` response; if no response within `dispatcher_state_timeout_ms` (default 2000), mark dispatcher as `UNRESPONSIVE` (not `active`). That directly fixes "dispatcher died 8 days ago but the coordinator still reports active".
   - Also add chassis link health subscription (`/chassis/link_health`) — but in multi-vehicle mode topic is namespaced. Hmm. Careful about legacy compat: subscribing to `/chassis/link_health` when multi-vehicle would be `/{vid}/chassis/link_health`. Might simply leave the chassis check in the gateway (which already subscribes to `/chassis/link_health` alone). Actually gateway only subscribes to the single topic.
